reference_note: Retain executable-code tutorial teaching. Visual models may vary; the owner accepts the present designed playback style for this episode. Do not force a live-IDE imitation.

visuals.bullets: Short supporting text paired with icons, diagrams or data; never a repeated text-only three-bullet template.
visuals.code_tutorial: Demonstrate open/edit or inspect code → run → inspect actual results/plots → return to relevant code. Keep source readable and highlight the active lines; do not simulate outputs.
visuals.branding: Reuse the approved transparent primary logo asset with a real alpha channel; do not use the opaque dark variant or a rectangular backing.

animation.default: Stationary content; animate only when motion explains a change in the data or a narrated process.
allowed: Data-grounded changes in graphs with clear labels and a visible meaning
Discrete highlight or reveal of a block, frame or step aligned with the narration
prohibited: Decorative continuous drifting, sliding labels or alignment movements
Numbers changing while the plotted result appears unchanged
Moving time-series selection boxes without an explained resampling step
Icons or locks popping in independently of the spoken explanation
animation.timing: Use actual narration cue times for conceptual focus steps; do not loop or move focus just to fill time.
animation.graph_counters: Show the final executed count unless successive intermediate states teach a visible, explained change. More bootstrap draws are not more independent cases.

visuals.screen_text: Keep explanations and scientific assumptions needed to interpret a result. Remove production/meta comments, defensive disclaimers such as this lesson does not fit a predictive model, and repetitive companion/source bookkeeping.
visuals.layout: Keep all cards, labels, arrows and notes inside the main white panel with consistent padding; inspect every discrete state. Consecutive scenes must add distinct content, not just change the title.
visuals.colour_semantics: Use colour consistently. Separate hierarchy and time-series examples; do not imply shared group identity through accidental colour reuse.

closing.speech_rate: Original natural speed, exactly 1.0; never time-stretch to fill the closing.
closing.silent_hold_scope: Final scene only, after the last spoken phrase.
closing.cta: Brief reference to GitHub materials or a verified open-access article in the description.
closing.cta_voice: A CTA may be spoken when already part of a future authorized script. Do not generate additional speech for this revision; retain its visual GitHub CTA.

audio.existing_approved_cleanup: apply once; never denoise an already-cleaned track again
